messages.subject: facet_wrap
parts:
Hadley,
I can say that I started to use R for lattice graphics a few years ago
and lately have had no need to use that package thanks to ggplot2,
even if lacking the new facet_wrap feature (which I have mimed by
cutting in pieces a many leveled factor) and being somewhat uneasy for
me for plot annotation without mapping to variables.
I have tried facet_wrap() and found regrettably that panel reordering
is not matched by strip text reordering, as can be seen by running the
example with different panel orders and comparing with facet_grid()

d <-ggplot(diamonds, aes(carat, price)) + xlim(0, 2) +stat_identity
()

vplayout <-function(x,y) viewport(layout.pos.row=x,layout.pos.col=y)

grid.newpage()
pushViewport(viewport(layout=grid.layout(2,1)))
print(
d+facet_wrap(~color,ncol=5)
,vp = vplayout(1,1))
print(
d+facet_wrap(~color2,ncol=5)
,vp = vplayout(2,1))

grid.newpage()
pushViewport(viewport(layout=grid.layout(2,1)))
print(
d+facet_grid(.~color)
,vp = vplayout(1,1))
print(
d+facet_grid(.~color2)
,vp = vplayout(2,1))


Regards
Filippo

excuse me,
I missed from the message the following first lines for the example of
facet_wrap

levels(diamonds$color)
[1] "D" "E" "F" "G" "H" "I" "J"
diamonds$color2 <-diamonds$color
diamonds$color2 <-factor(diamonds$color2, levels=c
('J','I','H','G','F','E','D'))
levels(diamonds$color2)
[1] 'J','I','H','G','F','E','D'

the fact I wished to point out was that panels reorder rightly
supplying a new order of levels, while strip texts don't

as with annotations, I think to have progressed a bit with the
grammar, thanks to a line in your recent book draft

Regards
Filippo
